questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Kavya invited all her friends, __isn’t it?__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**didn’t she?**'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is the incorrect use of the question tag "**isn’t it**".
 
• In the given sentence, the statement is positive, so the question tag should be negative.
 
• The correct negative question tag for "**invited**" (which is in the past tense) is "**didn’t she?**"

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 1: didn’t she?**’.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Kavya invited all her friends, **didn’t she?__***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **did she?**: This option is incorrect because it is not in the proper negative form for a question tag.
 
• **don’t she?**: This option is grammatically incorrect as it uses the present tense “don’t” with “she,” which should not be used together.
 
• **isn’t she?**: This option is incorrect because it does not match the past tense of the main statement and does not form a correct question tag.

questions.question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

This is the eldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.

options.text: This is the more older standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the most old standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the more elder standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the superlative form of the adjective 'oldest' should be used instead of 'eldest'.
 
• The word **'eldest'** is typically used for people, especially in the context of family relationships, while **'oldest'** is used for objects, structures, and other non-living things.
 
• Therefore, the correct form is 'oldest'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When discussing age or duration in the context of objects or structures, use **'oldest'** to indicate the greatest age.
 
• The word **'eldest'** is reserved for the oldest person among a group of people, typically within a family.
 
 
• **Example (correct usage of 'eldest'):** *She is the eldest of the three siblings.*
 
• **Example (correct usage of 'oldest'):** *This is the oldest tree in the park.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They decided to / travel in train / instead of driving / to New Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**travel in train**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase 'travel in train' is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be **'travel by train'** instead of **'travel in train'**.
 
• This is because the preposition **'by'** is used when referring to a mode of transportation.
 
• **Example:** *They decided to travel by train instead of driving to New Delhi.*

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *They decided to **travel by train** instead of driving to New Delhi.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the **subjects are both singular** and are **connected by** the words "not/but, not, or, nor, neither/nor, either/or, not only/but also, etc."" the **verb is singular**. 

 
 
• **Example:** ***Either Sita or Geeta is** to blame for the accident*.
 
 
 
• If the **subjects are both plurals** and are **connected by** the words "not/but, not, or, nor, neither/nor, either/or, not only/but also, etc."" the **verb is plural**. 
 
 
• Example: ***Not only dogs but also cats are** available at the shelter*.
